dedupe_keys.name: hhs office for civil rights breach portal breaches of protected health information affecting 500 or more individuals

description: The Breach Portal of the US Department of Health and Human Services lists every reported breach of patients' health information that affected 500 or more people, making it the main public record of cyber attacks, thefts and other failures that expose data held by hospitals, clinics, health insurers and their contractors. The producer is the department's Office for Civil Rights, which receives these reports under the HIPAA breach notification rule and investigates them. Coverage is national. Each entry gives the organisation, state, type of entity, number of individuals affected, submission date, type of breach such as hacking or unauthorised disclosure, where the data were held such as email or paper records, and whether a business associate was involved. The listing is available free on the portal without registration; a snapshot of 2013 to 2017 with 1,512 breaches affecting over 154 million records is also available as a CC0 CSV from Dryad. Caveats: only breaches of 500 or more individuals are listed publicly, entries describe data exposure, not service outages, and causes are coarse categories. Simulation uses: estimating the frequency and scale of cyber incidents in health care for risk models, and tracking the growth of hacking and ransomware. Related records: the Gaza hospital attacks data (data-gaza-attacks-on-hospitals-2023-2025) cover physical attacks on hospitals.
